# nullplatform_application (Resource)

The application resource allows you to manage a nullplatform Application. Destroying it asks the platform to delete the application (status `deleting`) and waits, up to the `delete` timeout, until the application's workflow has removed what it created. An application still being created (`pending_hook`, `pending`, `creating`) or updated (`updating`) cannot be deleted yet: destroy first waits for that to end, within the same timeout. One already `deleting` is waited for the same way.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    nullplatform = {
      source = "nullplatform/nullplatform"
    }
  }
}

provider "nullplatform" {}

variable "namespace_id" {
  description = "ID of the namespace that owns the application"
  type        = number
}

resource "nullplatform_application" "api" {
  name           = "my-api"
  namespace_id   = var.namespace_id
  repository_url = "https://github.com/my-org/my-api"

  tags = jsonencode({
    team = "platform"
  })

  settings = jsonencode({})
}

output "application_nrn" {
  value = nullplatform_application.api.nrn
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the application. Maximum length is 60 characters.
- `namespace_id` (Number) The ID of the namespace that owns this application.

### Optional

- `application_type_id` (String) The ID of the application type of this application (see `nullplatform_application_type`). The type must be active and visible in the application's namespace. It is set when the application is created and cannot be changed: a different type is a different application, and the platform does not give the name of a deleted application to a new one. When not set, it reads the type the platform holds: an application of a type imported, or managed from before this attribute, keeps its type. With a type, `repository_url` may be left out and arrive later from the type's workflow.
- `application_type_snapshot_id` (String) The ID of the snapshot of its type the application is on: its `attributes` pass that snapshot's schema. Empty for an application with no type. A change of the type's name, description or schema cuts a new snapshot and leaves the application on the one it has. Set it to move the application: to `nullplatform_application_type.<name>.last_snapshot_id` to keep it on the type's latest schema, or to an earlier snapshot of the type to go back. The move is one request together with `attributes`, and it is refused, changing nothing, when the attributes do not pass the destination's schema. A new application is created on the type's last snapshot, and the `attributes` it is created with must pass that snapshot's schema; one configured for another snapshot is moved there once its type's workflow has answered its creation, which the create waits for (`create` timeout). When not set, the application stays on its snapshot and this reads it.
- `attributes` (String) JSON string with the values of the fields of the application's type, checked against the type's schema. Only for an application with `application_type_id`. When set, it is the whole of them: only what changed is sent, and a key that is no longer here is removed from the application, also one that was set outside Terraform. A key written as `null` is a key left out, and a key the platform holds as `null` is removed. When not set, it reads what the platform holds (`{}` for an application with no type).
- `auto_deploy_on_creation` (Boolean) `True` if the application must be deployed immediately after being created, `false` otherwise.
- `is_mono_repo` (Boolean) `True` if the application shares the repository with other apps, `false` otherwise.
- `repository_app_path` (String) The folder where the application is located inside a monorepo.
- `repository_url` (String) The URL of the repository that holds this application. When not set, it reads what the platform holds: for an application of a type, the one the type's workflow reported when it created the application.
- `settings` (String) JSON string containing settings for the application.
- `slug` (String) A namespace-wide unique slug for the application.
- `status` (String) The status of the application. Possible values: [`pending_hook`, `pending`, `creating`, `updating`, `active`, `inactive`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`]. An application with no type starts as `pending`, and the platform's workflow makes it `creating`, then `active`. An application of a type starts as `pending_hook` and its type's workflow makes it `active` (or `failed`); until then the platform refuses every edit of it, and an update waits for it (`update` timeout). When the platform has no hook to send for the creation of an application of a type, it refuses the create, which fails with the platform's message.
- `tags` (String) JSON string containing tags for the application.
- `template_id` (Number) The ID of the template that was used to create this application.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `messages` (String) JSON string containing status messages for the application.
- `nrn` (String) The Nullplatform Resource Name (NRN) for the application.
